claims.text: The anti-farming check in POL-NS-07 trips on the driver's own trailing-window record: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 4, which is '4 or more', and 4 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, which is greater than the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs are therefore satisfied on the driver's own numbers, compensation must be WITHHELD, and the case must escalate under POL-NS-09(d); the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags (7) is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-30-day figure.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and replaces any monetary outcome: the Judge issues no monetary ruling and the disputed amount is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded. On the fare ledger's present state - cancellation_fee 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - that is the only disposition under which the rider is not left carrying the $4.50 while the platform reviews a driver with four no-show terminations in the last 30 days.

POL-NS-07 does more than withhold the driver's payout on these facts: it requires the escalation packet to DIRECT THE REVIEWER to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full. The file that goes to human review therefore carries a rider refund instruction on the $4.50, while the amount itself is held rather than collected or refunded by the automated pipeline in the interim.

The escalation on this file is driven entirely by the driver's pattern and not by any rider-abuse signal: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so the second limb of POL-NS-09(d) and the two-party limb of POL-NS-09(c) do not fire, and no limb of POL-NS-09 points back at this rider's own conduct.

claims.text: Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is met: the trip record for TRP-02727 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-07T22:40:11+08:00, sourced from platform telemetry, after the driver had been navigating to the registered pickup point since 22:33:03.

Limb (b) is met on the trace itself and needs no assertion of proximity. The derived arrival block reports a long qualifying in-geofence run beginning at 2026-09-07T22:40:11+08:00 - the exact second of the 'arrived' event - containing 49 qualifying fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the minimum distance from the pin anywhere in the derived driver track is 0.0 m. The arrival geofence test of POL-NS-02 is therefore satisfied, not failed, and the driver is deemed to have arrived.

Limb (c) is met with a wide margin: the effective in-geofence dwell is a single continuous run of 484 seconds, against a free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip, and the derived shortfall is -304 seconds. There is no shortfall, so POL-NS-06 has nothing to bite on and the waiting period the rider paid for was served in full.

Limb (d) is met: the record shows no boarding event, the trip was terminated by the driver at 2026-09-07T22:48:15+08:00 - 484 seconds after the dwell began - and the cancellation is recorded under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, so the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable.

The arrival marker is not a false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05. The first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the 'arrived' timestamp, so no admissible fix places the driver more than 300 m from the pin at the moment of the marker, and a single continuous in-geofence run of 49 fixes is inconsistent with an arrival tapped while driving through. Even if the marker were held false, limb (iii) preserves the fee: the clock recomputed from that same first qualifying in-geofence fix still yields a 484 second dwell, above the 180 second minimum, and any false-arrival record is a referral that never suppresses the money.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Limb (a) fails: the chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the driver at 22:40:31 ('im at the pickup point'), and nothing from the rider at all. Limb (c) is affirmatively failed rather than undecidable: the rider track is present with 83 fixes, not one of them within the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), the rider's device sitting roughly 697 m to 705 m from the pin throughout. POL-NS-11 therefore has no work to do here, and the clause cannot be run in the rider's favour.

POL-NS-03 is not engaged. That clause decides a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's fixes lie inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, the minimum distance to the pin across the derived driver track being 0.0 m. This is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case, and no goodwill payment or rider refund follows from it.

There is no fare defect to excuse the charge. The fare breakdown's cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 recorded on this trip, so the POL-NS-08(d) reconciliation is satisfied for the net figure, and the ledger shows SGD 4.50 charged with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. The amount the rider contests is the amount the schedule fixes.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee - SGD 3.60, which is the money block's own computed driver_compensation figure. I rely only on the two trailing-30-day fields the clause names, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the field this test reads. I disclose the one qualification on this record: both limbs of the anti-farming check are met (no_show_terminations_30d is 4, and 4 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, above 0.08), so compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). That is a routing consequence of the checker, not a finding that this trip was a farmed no-show, and escalation holds the fee rather than refunding it: this trip's own evidence - a 484 second continuous dwell inside a 50 m radius, a single unanswered driver message, and a rider device stationary some 700 m from the pin - describes a genuine no-show.

Whatever the routing of the compensation question, the rider's claim to have the SGD 4.50 returned is not supported on this evidence: no rider-exonerating clause of the no-show policy applies, so no refund is licensed. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative - on this rider-filed dispute it leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands, with the charge in place and refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, and it never restores a charge.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer and the SGD 4.50 no-show fee is held rather than collected or refunded while that review is pending. Neither of you moves money today.

On the trip itself, the driver's account is supported. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02727) shows the driver en route from 22:33, tapping 'I'm Here' at 22:40:11 and cancelling at 22:48:15 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02727) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 22:40:11 for one continuous 484-second run of 49 qualifying fixes. That satisfies POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d): arrival event present, geofence entry at that event, a 484-second dwell against the 180-second free waiting period, and termination under a recognised no-show code after the dwell elapsed. The arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05 (he was stationary at the pin, not driving past), POL-NS-06's shortfall rule has nothing to bite on, and POL-NS-03 does not apply because his fixes were inside the arrival radius, not outside it. The fare line of SGD 4.50 reconciles with the SGD 4.50 platform fee under POL-NS-08(d). The rider's exoneration route could not be run: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02727) holds a single driver message and none from the rider, and the rider's device sat roughly 700 m from the pin throughout, so POL-NS-04 fails at limbs (a) and (c). The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02727-01, weight 0.0) is not needed, because the dwell already exceeded the minimum.

That would ordinarily mean the fee stands and the driver is paid SGD 3.60, being 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee (the money block's own driver_compensation figure). I cannot process it. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips on the driver's own trailing-30-day numbers: no_show_terminations_30d is 4 (the test needs 4 or more) and 4 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, above the 0.08 rate limb. Those are the only two profile fields the clause reads; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter of 7 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and played no part. Compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d).

Escalation is terminal and replaces any monetary outcome. The driver's request that the charge simply stand (POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION) is displaced: NO_ACTION would leave the rider charged, whereas escalation holds the fee. The rider's request for a refund is not granted now either. POL-NS-07 directs the escalation packet to instruct the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.50 cancellation fee in full, and that instruction is recorded as a referral; the SGD 4.50 stays frozen meanwhile.

The reviewer must settle one open question: whether the driver's four no-show terminations in the last 30 days at a 0.10 rate reflect fee-farming, in which case the rider's fee is refunded in full, or whether this trip was a genuine no-show that the pattern alone should not distort. My confidence is 0.9; every artifact this finding rests on carries a weight multiplier of 1.0, so nothing is discounted and the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.
referrals: POL-NS-07: the escalation packet must direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.50 cancellation fee in full; the amount is held rather than collected or refunded meanwhile, as POL-NS-09 requires.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider, and to the driver: this case is escalated to a human reviewer. No money moves on the automated pipeline: your $4.50 stays held, neither collected nor refunded, until review. Per POL-NS-07 the reviewer is instructed to refund the $4.50 to the rider in full.

On the underlying no-show, the driver's account is made out on this record. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02727) shows the driver tap 'I'm Here' at 22:40:11 and the trip terminated by the driver at 22:48:15 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02727) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 22:40:11 - a single qualifying in-geofence run of 49 fixes lasting 484 seconds, minimum distance to the pin 0.0 m - so the dwell of 484 s comfortably exceeds the 180 s free waiting period in force. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. POL-NS-05 finds no false arrival marker: the marker coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and even recomputed the dwell still meets the minimum. POL-NS-06 has nothing to bite on (shortfall -304 s). POL-NS-03 is not engaged, the driver being inside the radius rather than at a wrong face of the venue within 400 m. POL-NS-08(d) is satisfied: the fare line of $4.50 reconciles with the platform_policy figure of $4.50, so no fare defect excuses the charge.

The rider is not exonerated by POL-NS-04. Limb (a) fails - the chat log (EV-CHAT-02727) holds one message, the driver's 'im at the pickup point' at 22:40:31, and nothing from the rider - and limb (c) is affirmatively failed, not undecidable: the rider track is present with 83 fixes and 0 of them within the 100 m presence radius, the device sitting roughly 700 m from the pin. POL-NS-11 accordingly has no work to do.

The outcome turns on the driver's own profile (EV-DPROF-02727). POL-NS-07 would fix the driver's payout at 80% of $4.50, i.e. $3.60, but the anti-farming check trips on both limbs: no_show_terminations_30d is 4 (at least 4) and 4 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, above the 0.08 rate limb. Compensation is therefore withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). Only the two trailing-30-day fields the clause names are used; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter mentioned in the debate is context only under POL-GEN-01 and decides nothing. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and replaces any monetary ruling, which is why the driver's further claim that the fee simply stand as NO_ACTION is outweighed: on this record the disposition of the fee is the held escalation, not a money ruling. The rider's points that the anti-farming trigger is driven by the driver's pattern and that no rider-abuse signal fires (no_show_disputes_30d 0) are accepted and consistent with this outcome. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02727-01 is MISSING and carries no fact; the limb it would support is unused because the dwell exceeded the minimum regardless.
referrals: POL-NS-07: the escalation packet must direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 in full; the driver's compensation of SGD 3.60 is withheld because the anti-farming check tripped (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 4 of completed_trips_30d 40 = 0.10, above 0.08).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The $4.50 no-show fee on trip TRP-02727 was properly incurred on the trip's own evidence. Driver DRV-09727 tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:40:11 and the GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second — 49 qualifying in-geofence fixes, minimum distance to the pin 0.0 m — and he held position continuously for 484 seconds (8 min 4 s) against the 180 second free waiting period, before cancelling at 22:48:15 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. That satisfies all four limbs of POL-NS-01, so the fee is chargeable. No rider-exonerating clause applies: the driver had arrived (POL-NS-02), and his stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, so POL-NS-03, which decides a driver stationary outside that radius but within 400 m, is not engaged; the only chat message was the driver's own at 22:40:31 and the rider's device sat about 700 m from the pin (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), so POL-NS-04 fails on both limb (a) and limb (c), and POL-NS-11 has nothing to answer; the arrival marker was not false (POL-NS-05, the first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the marker); and a 484 second dwell means no waiting-period shortfall (POL-NS-06, derived shortfall -304 s). POL-NS-10 does not apply because the driver, not the rider, cancelled. The rider's request to have the $4.50 returned is therefore not supported on the trip evidence.

The driver's payout cannot, however, be released automatically. DRV-09727's profile shows 4 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days and 40 completed trips, and 4 / 40 = 0.10, so both limbs of the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check are met (4 or more, and a rate above 0.08). Only the two fields POL-NS-07 names are used; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and decides nothing. Under POL-NS-07 compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). I accept both advocates' reading of this and it is the ground of the ruling.

ESCALATE is terminal: no monetary ruling issues, so amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are null, and the disputed $4.50 is placed on hold — neither collected nor refunded — while a human reviewer examines the driver's no-show pattern. The escalation packet carries the POL-NS-07 instruction to direct the reviewer to refund the rider's $4.50 in full if that pattern is confirmed; that instruction is recorded in referrals, not as money this ruling moves.

On confidence: every artifact that decides these facts carries weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown, driver profile), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory is absent (EV-ADVIS-02727-01, weight 0.0) but carries no deciding fact here: POL-NS-06(i) never had to be run, because this was a single continuous in-geofence dwell, not separate intervals to be summed.

The open question for the reviewer is whether DRV-09727's four 30-day no-show terminations indicate deliberate fee-farming or ordinary no-shows. This trip's own record describes a genuine no-show — a 484 second dwell inside a 50 m radius, a single unanswered driver message, and a rider device stationary roughly 700 m from the pin — and that is why the fee itself is not refunded by this ruling.

The chat log holds one message, sent by the driver at 22:40:31; nothing from you. Your own device's track sits about 700 m from the pickup pin throughout, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed and that clause cannot exonerate you, and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the driver's fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it. The SGD 4.50 fare line equals the trip's platform-policy cancellation fee, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. On those facts all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold and the fee is chargeable. Both limbs are met, so compensation is withheld and POL-NS-09(d) makes this case escalate. The rider's claims that the check trips and that escalation displaces any monetary outcome are accepted. The driver's claim that the outcome should be NO_ACTION leaving the charge in place is outweighed by that mandatory escalation. This is a routing consequence of the checker and not a finding on this trip, whose own evidence reads as a genuine no-show. The specific question for the reviewer is whether this driver's four no-show terminations in 30 days amount to fee-farming warranting the withheld payout and the refund described above — a pattern question a single-trip view cannot settle. Because this is ESCALATE, no monetary effect issues and the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold is not reached.

Limb (d) is met: the record shows no boarding event, the trip was terminated by the driver at 2026-09-07T22:48:15+08:00 - 484 seconds after the dwell began - and the cancellation is recorded under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, so the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable.

The arrival marker is not a false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05. The first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the 'arrived' timestamp, so no admissible fix places the driver more than 300 m from the pin at the moment of the marker, and a single continuous in-geofence run of 49 fixes is inconsistent with an arrival tapped while driving through. Even if the marker were held false, limb (iii) preserves the fee: the clock recomputed from that same first qualifying in-geofence fix still yields a 484 second dwell, above the 180 second minimum, and any false-arrival record is a referral that never suppresses the money.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Limb (a) fails: the chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the driver at 22:40:31 ('im at the pickup point'), and nothing from the rider at all. Limb (c) is affirmatively failed rather than undecidable: the rider track is present with 83 fixes, not one of them within the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0), the rider's device sitting roughly 697 m to 705 m from the pin throughout. POL-NS-11 therefore has no work to do here, and the clause cannot be run in the rider's favour.

POL-NS-03 is not engaged. That clause decides a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's fixes lie inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, the minimum distance to the pin across the derived driver track being 0.0 m. This is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case, and no goodwill payment or rider refund follows from it.

There is no fare defect to excuse the charge. The fare breakdown's cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 recorded on this trip, so the POL-NS-08(d) reconciliation is satisfied for the net figure, and the ledger shows SGD 4.50 charged with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. The amount the rider contests is the amount the schedule fixes.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee - SGD 3.60, which is the money block's own computed driver_compensation figure. I rely only on the two trailing-30-day fields the clause names, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the field this test reads. I disclose the one qualification on this record: both limbs of the anti-farming check are met (no_show_terminations_30d is 4, and 4 divided by completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.10, above 0.08), so compensation is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). That is a routing consequence of the checker, not a finding that this trip was a farmed no-show, and escalation holds the fee rather than refunding it: this trip's own evidence - a 484 second continuous dwell inside a 50 m radius, a single unanswered driver message, and a rider device stationary some 700 m from the pin - describes a genuine no-show.

ledger.claim: Whatever the routing of the compensation question, the rider's claim to have the SGD 4.50 returned is not supported on this evidence: no rider-exonerating clause of the no-show policy applies, so no refund is licensed. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative - on this rider-filed dispute it leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands, with the charge in place and refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, and it never restores a charge.
